readings.title: The Sign of Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz
readings.subtitle: The Swift Spoil and the Rushing Flood
readings.text: [Isaiah 8:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Take a large tablet, and write on it with a man’s pen concerning Mahěr-Shalal-Ḥash-Baz.</dq> [2] <dq>“And let <dn>Me</dn> take reliable witnesses to record, Uriyah the priest and Zeḵaryahu son of Yeḇereḵyahu.”</dq> [3] And <dn>I</dn> went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Call <dn>את</dn> his name Mahěr-Shalal-Ḥash-Baz;</dq> [4] <dq>for before the child knows to cry ‘<dn>My</dn> father’ and ‘<dn>My</dn> mother,’ the riches of Dammeseq and the spoil of Shomeron is taken away before the sovereign of Ashshur.”</dq> [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to me again, saying, [6] <dq>“Inasmuch as these people refused <dn>את</dn> the waters of Shiloaḥ that flow softly, and rejoice in Retsin and in Remalyahu’s son;</dq> [7] <dq>now therefore, see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings up over them <dn>את</dn> the waters of the River, strong and mighty – <dn>את</dn> the sovereign of Ashshur and <dn>את</dn> all his esteem. And he shall come up over all his channels and go over all his banks.</dq> [8] <dq>“And he shall pass through Yehuḏah, he shall overflow and pass over, reaching up to the neck. And the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of <dn>Your</dn> land, O Immanu’ěl.</dq> [9] <dq>“Be shattered, O you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Give ear, all you from the far places of the earth. Gird yourselves, but be broken in pieces; gird yourselves, but be broken in pieces.</dq> [10] <dq>“Take counsel, and it comes to naught; speak a word, and it does not stand, for <dn>Ěl</dn> is with us.”</dq>

readings.title: A Call to Fear YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Stumbling Stone and the Sealed Torah
readings.text: [Isaiah 8:11] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke thus to me with a strong hand, and instructed me that <dn>I</dn> should not walk in the way of this people, saying, [12] <dq>“Do not say, ‘A conspiracy,’ concerning all that this people call a conspiracy, nor be afraid of their threats, nor be troubled.</dq> [13] <dq>“<dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dn>Him</dn> you shall set apart. Let <dn>Him</dn> be your fear, and let <dn>Him</dn> be your dread.</dq> [14] <dq>“And <dn>He</dn> shall be for a set-apart place, but a stone of stumbling and a rock that makes for falling to both the houses of Yisra’ěl, as a trap and a snare to the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.</dq> [15] <dq>“And many among them shall stumble and fall, and be broken and snared and taken.”</dq> [16] <dq>Bind up the witness, seal the Torah among <dn>My</dn> taught ones.</dq> [17] And <dn>I</dn> shall wait on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who hides <dn>His</dn> face from the house of Ya‛aqoḇ. And <dn>I</dn> shall look for <dn>Him</dn>. [18] Look, <dn>I</dn> and the children whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given me – for signs and wonders in Yisra’ěl from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, who dwells in Mount Tsiyon. [19] And when they say to you, “Seek those who are mediums and wizards, who whisper and mutter,” should not a people seek their <dn>Elohim</dn>? Should they seek the dead on behalf of the living? [20] To the Torah and to the witness! If they do not speak according to this Word, it is because they have no daybreak. [21] And they shall pass through it hard pressed and hungry. And it shall be, when they are hungry, that they shall be wroth and curse their sovereign and their <dn>Elohim</dn>, looking upward. [22] And they shall look to the earth and see distress and darkness, gloom of hard times, and be driven into thick darkness.

readings.title: The People in Darkness See a Great Light
readings.subtitle: For Unto Us a Child Is Born
readings.text: [Isaiah 9:1] But there is no gloom upon her who is distressed, as when at first <dn>He</dn> humbled <dn>את</dn> the land of Zeḇulun and <dn>את</dn> the land of Naphtali, and afterward more heavily oppressed her, by the way of the sea, beyond the Yarděn, in Galil of the nations. [2] The people who were walking in darkness have seen a great light; upon those who dwelt in the land of the shadow of death a light has shone. [3] <dn>You</dn> shall increase the nation; <dn>You</dn> shall make its joy great. They shall rejoice before <dn>You</dn>, as in the joy of harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the spoil. [4] For <dn>You</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> the yoke of his burden and <dn>את</dn> the staff of his shoulder, <dn>את</dn> the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Miḏyan. [5] For every boot of one trampling in tumult, and coat rolled in blood, shall be used for burning and fuel of fire. [6] For a Child is born unto us, a Son is given unto us, and the rule is on <dn>His</dn> shoulder. And <dn>His</dn> Name is called Wonder, Counsellor, Strong <dn>Ěl</dn>, Father of Continuity, Prince of Peace. [7] Of the increase of <dn>His</dn> rule and peace there is no end, upon the throne of Daviḏ and over <dn>His</dn> reign, to establish it and sustain it with right-ruling and with righteousness from now on, even forever. The ardour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts does this.

readings.title: Judgment on Arrogant Israel
readings.subtitle: His Hand Is Stretched Out Still
readings.text: [Isaiah 9:8] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a word against Ya‛aqoḇ, and it has fallen on Yisra’ěl. [9] And the people shall know, all of them, Ephrayim and the inhabitant of Shomeron, who say in pride and greatness of heart: [10] “The bricks have fallen down, but we rebuild with hewn stones; the sycamores are cut down, but we replace them with cedars.” [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> set up <dn>את</dn> the adversaries of Retsin against him, and stirred up <dn>את</dn> his enemies, [12] the Arameans before and the Philistines behind. And they devour <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl with an open mouth. With all this <dn>His</dn> displeasure has not turned back, and <dn>His</dn> hand is still stretched out. [13] And the people have not turned back to <dn>Him</dn> who strikes them, nor have they sought <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> cuts off head and tail from Yisra’ěl, palm branch and reed in one day. [15] Elder and highly respected, he is the head; the prophet who teaches falsehood, he is the tail. [16] For the leaders of this people lead them astray, and those who are guided by them are swallowed up. [17] Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not rejoice over their young men, and has no compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is defiled and evil, and every mouth speaks foolishness. With all this <dn>His</dn> displeasure has not turned back, and <dn>His</dn> hand is still stretched out. [18] For wrongness burns as the fire; it consumes thornbushes and weeds, and sets the bushes of the forest ablaze, and they roll up like rising smoke. [19] The land shall be burned up by the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, and the people be as fuel for the fire. A man shall not spare his brother, [20] and cut down on the right hand, but shall be hungry; and he devours on the left hand, but shall not be satisfied; each one devouring the flesh of his own arm: [21] Menashsheh <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim, and Ephrayim <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh; together they are against Yehuḏah. With all this <dn>His</dn> displeasure has not turned back, and <dn>His</dn> hand is still stretched out. [Isaiah 10:1] <dq>“Woe to those making unrighteous inscriptions, and writers who have prescribed toil,</dq> [2] <dq>to keep the needy back from right-ruling, and to take what is right from the poor of <dn>My</dn> people, that widows become their prey, and orphans their plunder.</dq> [3] <dq>“What shall you do in the day of visitation, and in the ruin which comes from afar? To whom would you run for help? And where would you leave your wealth?</dq> [4] <dq>“Without <dn>Me</dn> they shall bow down among the prisoners, and fall among the killed.”</dq> With all this <dn>His</dn> displeasure has not turned back, and <dn>His</dn> hand is still stretched out.

readings.title: Woe to Assyria, the Rod of Anger
readings.subtitle: The Arrogant Axe Will Be Judged
readings.text: [Isaiah 10:5] <dq>“Woe to Ashshur, the rod of <dn>My</dn> displeasure and the staff in whose hand is <dn>My</dn> displeasure.</dq> [6] <dq>“Against a defiled nation <dn>I</dn> send him, and against the people of <dn>My</dn> wrath <dn>I</dn> command him to seize the spoil, to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mud of the streets.</dq> [7] <dq>“But he does not intend so, nor does his heart think so, for it is in his heart to destroy, and cut off not a few nations.</dq> [8] <dq>“For he says, ‘Are not my princes sovereigns?</dq> [9] <dq>Is not Kalno like Karkemish? Is not Ḥamath like Arpaḏ? Is not Shomeron like Dammeseq?</dq> [10] <dq>As my hand has found the reigns of the idols, whose carved images excelled those of Yerushalayim and Shomeron,</dq> [11] <dq>as <dn>I</dn> have done to Shomeron and her idols, do <dn>I</dn> not do also to Yerushalayim and her idols?’</dq> [12] <dq>“And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has performed all <dn>His</dn> work on Mount Tsiyon and on Yerushalayim, that <dn>I</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> the fruit of the greatness of the heart of the sovereign of Ashshur, and <dn>את</dn> the boasting of his haughty looks.</dq> [13] <dq>“For he has said, ‘By the power of my hand <dn>I</dn> have done it, and by my wisdom, for <dn>I</dn> have been clever. And <dn>I</dn> remove the boundaries of the people, and have robbed their treasuries. And <dn>I</dn> put down the inhabitants like a strong one.</dq> [14] <dq>And my hand finds the riches of the people like a nest. And <dn>I</dn> have gathered <dn>את</dn> all the earth like forsaken eggs are gathered. And there was no one who moved his wing, nor opened his mouth with even a peep.’ ”</dq> [15] Would the axe boast itself over him who chops with it, or the saw exalt itself over him who saws with it? As a rod waving those who lift it up! As a staff lifting up that which is not wood! [16] Therefore the Master, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, sends leanness among his fat ones. And under his esteem he kindles a burning like the burning of a fire. [17] And the Light of Yisra’ěl shall be for a fire, and his Set-apart One for a flame. And it shall burn and devour his weeds and his thornbushes in one day, [18] and consume <dn>את</dn> the esteem of his forest and of his fertile field, both life and flesh. And they shall be as when a sick man wastes away, [19] and the remaining trees of his forest shall be so few in number that a child records them.

readings.title: The Remnant of Israel Will Return
readings.subtitle: The Destruction of the Assyrian Host
readings.text: [Isaiah 10:20] And in that day it shall be that the remnant of Yisra’ěl, and those who have escaped of the house of Ya‛aqoḇ, never again lean upon him who struck them, but shall lean upon <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, in truth. [21] A remnant shall return, the remnant of Ya‛aqoḇ, to the Mighty <dn>Ěl</dn>. [22] For though your people, O Yisra’ěl, be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return – a decisive end, overflowing with righteousness. [23] For the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is making a complete end, as decided, in the midst of all the earth. [24] Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“<dn>My</dn> people, who dwell in Tsiyon, be not afraid of Ashshur, who struck you with a rod and lifts up his staff against you, in the way of Mitsrayim.</dq> [25] <dq>“For yet a little while and the displeasure shall be completed, and <dn>My</dn> displeasure be to their destruction.”</dq> [26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts stirs up a lash for him as the smiting of Miḏyan at the rock of Orěḇ. And as <dn>His</dn> rod was on the sea, so shall <dn>He</dn> lift it up in the way of Mitsrayim. [27] And in that day it shall be that his burden is removed from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil. [28] He has come upon Ayath, he has passed Miḡron. At Miḵmash he stored his supplies. [29] They have gone through the pass, they have taken up lodging at Geḇa. Ramah is afraid, Giḇ‛ah of Sha’ul has fled. [30] Lift up your voice, O daughter of Galliym! Listen, Layishah – O poor Anathoth! [31] Maḏměnah has fled, the inhabitants of Gěḇim sought refuge. [32] Yet he remains at Noḇ that day; he shakes his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Tsiyon, the hill of Yerushalayim. [33] Look, the Master, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, is lopping off a branch with an awesome crash, and the tall ones are cut down, and the lofty ones are laid low. [34] And <dn>He</dn> shall cut down <dn>את</dn> the thickets of the forest with iron, and Leḇanon shall fall as a mighty one!

readings.title: The Righteous Reign of the Branch
readings.subtitle: The Root of Jesse and the Restored Remnant
readings.text: [Isaiah 11:1] And a Rod shall come forth from the stump of Yishai, and a Sprout from his roots shall be fruitful. [2] The Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall rest upon <dn>Him</dn> – the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [3] and shall make <dn>Him</dn> breathe in the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> shall not judge by the sight of <dn>His</dn> eyes, nor decide by the hearing of <dn>His</dn> ears. [4] But with righteousness <dn>He</dn> shall judge the poor, and shall decide with straightness for the meek ones of the earth, and shall strike <dn>את</dn> the earth with the rod of <dn>His</dn> mouth, and slay the wrong with the breath of <dn>His</dn> lips. [5] And righteousness shall be the girdle of <dn>His</dn> loins, and trustworthiness the girdle of <dn>His</dn> waist. [6] And a wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and a leopard lie down with the young goat, and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together, and a little child leads them. [7] And cow and bear shall feed, their young ones lie down together, and a lion eat straw like an ox. [8] And the nursing child shall play by the cobra’s hole, and the weaned child shall put his hand in the adder’s den. [9] <dq>They do no evil nor destroy in all <dn>My</dn> set-apart mountain, for the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> as the waters cover the sea.</dq> [10] And in that day there shall be a Root of Yishai, standing as a banner to the people. Unto <dn>Him</dn> the nations shall seek, and <dn>His</dn> rest shall be esteem. [11] And it shall be in that day that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sets <dn>His</dn> hand again a second time to recover <dn>את</dn> the remnant of <dn>His</dn> people who are left, from Ashshur and from Mitsrayim, from Pathros and from Kush, from Ěylam and from Shin‛ar, from Ḥamath and from the islands of the sea. [12] And <dn>He</dn> shall raise a banner for the nations, and gather <dn>את</dn> the outcasts of Yisra’ěl, and assemble <dn>את</dn> the dispersed of Yehuḏah from the four corners of the earth. [13] And the envy of Ephrayim shall turn aside, and the adversaries of Yehuḏah be cut off. Ephrayim shall not envy Yehuḏah, and Yehuḏah not trouble Ephrayim. [14] But they shall fly down upon the shoulder of the Philistines toward the west; together they plunder <dn>את</dn> the people of the east, their hand stretching forth on Eḏom and Mo’aḇ, and the children of Ammon shall be subject to them. [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall put under the ban <dn>את</dn> the tongue of the Sea of Mitsrayim, and <dn>He</dn> shall wave <dn>His</dn> hand over the River with the might of <dn>His</dn> Spirit, and shall strike it in the seven streams, and shall cause men to tread it in sandals. [16] And there shall be a highway for the remnant of <dn>His</dn> people, those left from Ashshur, as it was for Yisra’ěl in the day when he came up from the land of Mitsrayim.
